answers.Q1: A data structure is a way of organizing and storing data in a computer so that it can be accessed and used efficiently. Types of data structure: Linear data structure - In these structures, data elements are arranged one after another in a sequence. Each element has a direct previous and next element, except the first and last one. Examples: array, linked list, stack, and queue. Non-linear data structure - In these structures data is not arranged in a single sequence. One element may connect to multiple other elements. Examples: trees and graph. Trees: A hierarchical structure with a root and child nodes.
answers.Q2: An algorithm is a finite set of step by step instructions used to solve a problem or perform a task. It takes input, processes it according to a logical sequence and produces output. Characteristics of good algorithm: A good algorithm should have the following characteristics. 1. Input: An algorithm may take zero or more inputs. Inputs are the value or data given to the algorithm for processing. 2. Output: An algorithm should produce at least one output. The output is the result of the computation or solution to the problem. 3. Finiteness: An algorithm must end after a finite number of steps. It should not run forever. 4. Definiteness: Each step of the algorithm should be clear, precise and unambiguous. There should be no confusion about what to do next. 5. Correctness: The algorithm should always give the correct result for valid input.
answers.Q3: Complexity analysis is the process of measuring the efficiency of an algorithm. It tells us how much time and memory an algorithm requires as the size of the input increases. It is used to compare different algorithms and determine which one is better for a specific task. Types of complexity: The two main types of complexity are 1. Time Complexity: Time complexity measures the amount of time taken by an algorithm to complete its execution. It describes how the running time increases as the input size increases. 2. Space Complexity: Space complexity measures the amount of memory used by an algorithm during execution. It includes memory used for variables, data structures, recursion and temporary storage. Some algorithms need extra memory to work efficiently, while others use very little additional memory.
answers.Q4: Array: An array is a linear data structure that stores elements of the same data type in contiguous memory locations. Each element can be accessed directly using an index number. Arrays are very useful when we need fast access to elements by position. Features: Elements are stored in continuous memory location. All elements must be of same type. Accessing an element is fast because of indexing. Insertion and deletion in the middle may be costly because shifting is required. Linked List: A linked list is a linear data structure made up of nodes. Each node contains two parts: Data - The actual value; Link/Pointer - A reference to the next node. Unlike arrays, linked list nodes are not stored in contiguous memory location. Instead, they are connected using link. Features: Memory is not required to be contiguous. Size can grow or shrink dynamically. Insertion and deletion are easier than in arrays.
